meta_description: Supply Chain Risk & Continuity — composed architecture, platform stack and the metric the program answers to.

blocks.x: A no-theater description of Supply Chain Risk & Continuity: what ships first, what it touches at operational stores, how it is verified, and the per workflow metric we commit to moving against baseline.
The problem this solution exists for
Multi-tier supply is opaque; disruptions surface as missed deliveries; re-planning takes weeks; ESG/provenance obligations add evidence duties.
Our approach

We build the risk-sensing control tower: multi-tier supplier telemetry, disruption early warning with scenario playbooks, autonomous re-planning within policy, and the provenance/evidence layer for regulated claims.
Reference architecture

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Supply Chain Risk & Continuity
blocks.note: The pipeline is measured end to end; each stage reports its own freshness and cost, which is what makes the unit economics arguable.

blocks.x: The architecture for Supply Chain Risk & Continuity is deliberately auditable: every stage exposes its inputs, its owner and its failure policy, and the decision path shares a timeline with the audit path. Nothing important happens off the record.
Components
Platform stack

Every item in the Supply Chain Risk & Continuity stack earns its place on measured cost and performance, not on vendor momentum. Where a component is already serving you well, we integrate it instead of replacing it.
How it runs in an engagement

items: We measure the starting position and lock the baseline with your team — no build work begins before the number is agreed.
A bounded pilot on your real data, with the gate review scheduled before the first commit is written.
Runbooks, enablement and the control trail that let your teams operate it without us in the room.
Quarterly re-audits and a ranked backlog of the next decisions worth automating — value that accumulates on purpose.

blocks.x: Prerequisites and data readiness

Before Supply Chain Risk & Continuity starts, three things need to exist: a metric your board recognizes, data access under an approved path, and a named owner on each source system. The readiness check takes two weeks and says no when it should.
How a delivery runs

The rhythm for Supply Chain Risk & Continuity: measure first, prove on real data, industrialize what survived the gate, and review the delta every fortnight with the people accountable for the number.
Outcomes we commit to
